answer: For a poll on a quartz sculpture by the harbor ledge, the server checks election-bound signatures against a frozen roster divided into three-key panels. It rejects invalid or repeat ballots and gives a panel one vote only if all three keys vote for the same option; otherwise it abstains. If all honest voters oppose an option, gaining a panel vote for it requires control of three keys, potentially costing recruitment effort. Shared keys enable abuse, and dissenting panels lose representation.
